sources.title: useFetch executable fake-hook lifecycle and request-order validation
useFetch params candidate independent source-first review

claims.text: The preserved source only requires automatic refetch when params changes; the hook signature, request library, equality semantics, cache behavior and UI policy are not preserved source constraints.

React compares each Effect dependency to its previous value with Object.is and runs cleanup before the next setup when dependencies change; object dependencies recreated each render can cause extra reruns.

Under the declared request(params,{signal}) contract, independent executable harnesses verify same/new identity behavior, cleanup abort, stale-write prevention, current-result acceptance and error handling.

findings: The preserved source is a singleton React coding question that only adds automatic refetch when params changes; it does not preserve the prior useFetch signature, request transport, deep-equality semantics, caching policy or stale-data UI policy.
The candidate keeps those missing details answer-side by declaring a stable request(params,{signal}) Promise contract and immutable params replacement as the trigger semantics.

The dependency explanation matches the current React useEffect reference: dependencies are compared with Object.is, changed dependencies cause old cleanup before new setup, and recreated object dependencies can cause extra reruns.
The implementation includes every reactive value it reads in the dependency array ([request, params]) and explicitly warns that an unstable request function would itself cause refetches.
The executable writer harness and a separately written reviewer harness both verify mount, same-identity, new-identity, in-place-mutation and cleanup behavior under the declared dependency model.

The stale-response race is handled by both AbortController and an active flag, so an obsolete request cannot overwrite the current params result even when the request implementation does not honor cancellation.
The answer does not invent project experience and does not present JSON.stringify(params) as a universal deep-comparison solution.
